scope: CPU BF16-boundary/FP32-accumulation diagnostic, not native BF16, CUDA or TT execution; does not replace FP32 acceptance gates
input_scope: Same real-poster conditions, dedicated seed-123 noise, pretrained weights and original 12-step occupancy sampler as paired TT runs. Strict fixture identity verified for every comparison.
finding: CPU BF16-boundary/FP32-product diagnostic differs 41.5% in final latent from FP32, but common FP32 decoder occupancy IoU is 0.868. Stock/real-RoPE TT differ 71.2%/71.7% from this diagnostic, with occupancy IoU only 0.540/0.536. A substantial mismatch persists against precision-aware references; do not explain all TT/FP32 drift as intended quantization. Errors are not additive components.
decision: Keep numerical gates and candidate defaults unchanged. Isolate backend normalization/attention/MLP arithmetic with identical learned activations. CPU diagnostic remains neither a CUDA oracle nor direct reconstruction-quality proof.
reproduce: python experiments/tenstorrent/precision_reference.py --stage ss --flow-inputs /path/to/poster-inputs/inputs.pt --threads 16 --output-dir /path/to/new; compare its trajectory to the sealed FP32 reference and both TT payloads, then use compare_occupancy.py with the same CPU decoder.
